vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security fixes are forced through even where a rule below (or the org-wide 'no major updates' rule) disables regular updates.

lockFileMaintenance.description: Refresh poetry.lock weekly so transitive dependencies get security fixes. Renovate only bumps dependencies declared in pyproject.toml, so indirect deps would otherwise stay pinned to a vulnerable version.

packageRules.description: Pin the Python constraint so Renovate resolves poetry.lock with a matching interpreter. requires-python lives in [project] (PEP 621) but the poetry manager reads [tool.poetry.dependencies].python, so it extracts nothing and lock updates silently fail.
Same as above, for the notebook scheduler (requires-python ^3.11)
Keep Scala on the 2.12 line - the jobs build against Spark _2.12 artifacts, and 2.13 is only a minor bump so it is not caught by the no-majors rule
Keep Spark on the 3.5 line - these jobs run inside the iomete Spark 3.5 images

Don't bump Spark in the lakehouse backup job - sparkVersion in its gradle.properties is the single source of truth for both the jars and the iomete/spark base image tag it runs on, so a bump here silently mismatches the runtime (see the revert of #277)
Don't touch antlr4-runtime - the forced version has to match what Spark pulls in, otherwise SQL parsing breaks at runtime
Move the Quarkus platform BOM, Gradle plugin and the forced quarkus-core version together so they stay consistent
Security fixes only for the vendored Debezium fork - it is pinned to Debezium 1.9 / Quarkus 2.16 / Spark 3.2 and has no CI, so routine bumps would just be broken PRs
